course_name_original: Atoomtheorie, chemische periodiciteit en chemische binding
course_name_en: Atomic Theory, Chemical Periodicity and Chemical Bonding
prerequisites: Basic principles of chemistry and chemical bonding as introduced in 'General and Technical Chemistry' (B-KUL-H01A8A).

learning_outcomes.text: Discuss early atomic models and the characteristics of atomic spectra of classical atomic structures.
Understand the problems with classical models (hydrogen spectrum, black body radiation, Planck's quantum).
Explain Bohr's classical model for a one-electron system and calculate orbital energies.
Identify shortcomings of the Bohr model, including the discussion of the photoelectric effect, wave-particle duality, and the de Broglie formula.
Derive the Schroedinger equation and solutions for the hydrogen atom.
Interpret wave functions and orbitals.
Explain Pauli's spin formalism.
Understand the concept of many-electron systems and the resulting Aufbau principle.
Know the concept of valence electrons and the resulting structure of the Periodic Table.
Be able to explain the periodically varying properties in the Periodic Table and their relationship to wave functions.
Understand the concepts of atomic and ionic radii.
Identify ionization energies, electron affinities, and electronegativity of different elements.
Understand the connections between electronegativity, orbital energies, and main types of bonds.
Better understand the concepts of electrostatic interactions, lattice energies, and Madelung summation.
Explain the stoichiometry, geometry, crystal structure, and stability of ionic bonds.
Be able to apply the concept of the Born-Haber cycle.
Be able to apply Lewis structures and understand their limits.
Construct atomic geometries using the VSEPR model.
Understand concepts of valence bond theory and apply simple hybridization schemes.
Understand the concept of multiple bonds, including sigma and pi bonds.
Know the principles of molecular orbital (MO) theory, starting with a good understanding of the Helium+ ion and its wave function.
Be able to explain the principles of LCAO and the resulting concepts of bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals and their energy levels.
Discuss the different MO types and their symmetry with homonuclear diatomic molecules.
Explain the difference between the MO structure of oxygen and nitrogen using the concept of s-p mixing.
For heteroatomic MOs, understand the importance of orbital energies and the relationship to electronegativity.
Be able to explain the variation principle.
Understand the delocalized view of chemical bonding in MO theory.
Apply the principles discussed above to polyatomic molecules and discuss the structure of H2O.
Understand the concepts of the Hückel model for conjugated molecules.
Understand the classical approach of a bonding electron gas.
Be able to develop the energy band diagram using a quantum mechanical approach.
Explain the difference between metals, semiconductors, and insulators.
Understand intrinsic semiconductors and p- and n-type semiconductors.
Apply this knowledge to the photovoltaic cell, the semiconductor diode – LED.
Understand crystal field theory and its shortcomings.
Understand the principles of ligand field theory, its relation to MO theory, and the resulting concept of the spectrochemical series.

syllabus_topics: Discussion of early atomic models and the characteristics of atomic spectra of classical atomic structures
Problems with classical models (hydrogen spectrum, black body radiation, Planck's quantum)
Bohr's classical model for a one-electron system and orbital energies
Shortcomings of the Bohr model, photoelectric effect, wave-particle duality, and the de Broglie formula
Derivation of the Schroedinger equation and solutions for the hydrogen atom
Interpretation of wave functions and orbitals
Pauli's spin formalism
Multiple-electron systems and the Aufbau principle
Valence electrons and the structure of the Periodic Table
Periodically varying properties in the Periodic Table and their relation to wave functions:
Atomic and ionic radii
Ionization energy, electron affinity, and electronegativity
Electronegativity, orbital energies, and main types of bonds
Ionic bonding:
Electrostatic interactions, lattice energies, and Madelung summation
Stoichiometry, geometry, crystal structure, and stability of ionic bonds
The Born-Haber cycle
Covalent bonding:
Classical Lewis structures and their limits
VSEPR model
Valence bond theory and hybridization
Multiple bonds, sigma and pi bond
Molecular-orbital (MO) theory
The Helium+ ion and its wave functions
LCAO, bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals and energy levels
Homonuclear diatomic molecules
MO types and symmetry
Oxygen, nitrogen, and s-p mixing
Heteroatomic MOs
Orbital energies and electronegativity
Variation principle
Delocalized view of chemical bonding
Application of these principles to polyatomic molecules: H2O
The Hückel model
Bonding in metals and semiconductors:
Classical approach: electron gas bonding
Development of the energy band diagram in the quantum mechanical approach
Difference between metals - semiconductors - insulators
Intrinsic semiconductors and p- and n-type semiconductors
Applications: the photovoltaic cell - the semiconductor diode - LED
Coordination complexes:
Crystal field theory and its shortcomings
Ligand field theory and the spectrochemical series

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with open questions and short calculations

assessment_rules: The written exam consists of approximately 7-10 open questions and short calculations, which must be answered and solved (closed book). Only a simple calculator from the list of approved devices may be used. If the evaluation shows that the student has insufficiently achieved one or more objectives of the course unit, the overall result may deviate from the weighted average of the components. The resit exam format is identical to the first examination opportunity.
